The entity should prohibit and sanction the creation and use of ad-hoc wireless networks, including the connecting of unapproved wireless base-stations to the entity’s core data network.
The entity should put in place mechanisms that allow for the identification and isolation of rogue wireless access points.
Authentication controls should be implemented to control access to wireless networks. The entity should consider a number of actions to limit unauthorized use of wireless communications outside its boundaries include, for example:
a. reducing the power of wireless transmissions so that the transmissions are less likely to emit a signal that can be used by adversaries outside of the physical perimeters of entities.
b. employing measures such as TEMPEST to control wireless emanations.
c. using directional/beam forming antennas that reduce the likelihood that unintended receivers will be able to intercept signals.
Prior to taking such actions, entities can conduct periodic wireless surveys to understand the radio frequency profile of its information systems as well as other systems that may be operating in the area.

controls.title: Web Filtering
controls.description: The entity shall manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) identify the types of websites to which personnel should or should not have access.
2) restrict access to websites that contain illegal information or are known to contain viruses or phishing material.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: identify the types of websites to which personnel should or should not have access.
The entity shall: restrict access to websites that contain illegal information or are known to contain viruses or phishing material.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P3. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): new control.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.23; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SC-7; ISRv3: none listed.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should reduce the risks of its personnel accessing websites that contain illegal information or are known to contain viruses or phishing material. A technique for achieving this works by blocking the IP address or domain of the website(s) concerned. Some browsers and anti-malware technologies do this automatically or can be configured to do so.
The entity should identify the types of websites to which personnel should or should not have access. The entity should consider blocking access to the following types of websites:
a. websites that have an information upload function unless permitted for valid business reasons.
b. known or suspected malicious websites (e.g. those distributing malware or phishing contents).
c. command and control servers.
d. malicious website acquired from threat intelligence.
e. websites sharing illegal content.
Prior to deploying this control, the entity should establish rules for the safe and appropriate use of online resources, including any restriction to undesirable or inappropriate websites and web-based applications. The rules should be kept up to date.
Training should be given to personnel on the secure and appropriate use of online resources including access to the web. The training should include the entity’s rules, contact point for raising security concerns, and exception process when restricted web resources need to be accessed for legitimate business reasons. Training should also be given to personnel to ensure that they do not overrule any browser advisory that reports that a website is not secure but allows the user to proceed.

controls.title: Identity and Access Management Policy
controls.description: The entity shall document and approve an identity and access management policy based on business and security requirements.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall document and approve an identity and access management policy based on business and security requirements.

Sub-Controls:
1) The identity and access management policy shall be documented and include the following requirements for:
   • Identity management
   • User access management
   • Access rights review
   • Privileged access management
   • Secure authentication
   • Password management
assessment_criteria: The identity and access management policy shall be documented and include the following requirements for: • Identity management • User access management • Access rights review • Privileged access management • Secure authentication • Password management
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.1.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: none listed; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-1; ISRv3: 5.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Owners of information and other associated assets should determine information security and business requirements related to identity and access management. A policy on identity and access management should be defined which takes account of these requirements and should be communicated to all relevant interested parties.
These requirements and the policy should consider the following:
a. determining which entities require which type of access to the information and other associated assets.
b. applications are secure and that access to them is controlled.
c. manage physical entry, ensuring secure access to physical locations where information and assets are stored.
d. apply the need-to-know principle, consider information security levels, and classify information accordingly to control dissemination and access.
e. restrict privileged accounts to essential personnel only, enforce strict access controls, regularly review permissions, and monitor all activities to prevent unauthorized access and misuse.
f. segregation of duties, separate the roles access requests, authorization, and administration.
g. relevant legislation, regulations and any contractual obligations regarding limitation of access to data or services.
h. implement continuous monitoring and logging for all account activities to detect and respond.

controls.title: Identity Management
controls.description: The entity shall manage the full lifecycle of the identities.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall manage the full lifecycle of the identities.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) assign a unique identifier to each user.
2) disable or remove user identities promptly when they are no longer needed.
3) create a separate account for each individual requiring access and prohibit account sharing among users.
4) log all activities associated with restricted identities.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: assign a unique identifier to each user.
The entity shall: disable or remove user identities promptly when they are no longer needed.
The entity shall: create a separate account for each individual requiring access and prohibit account sharing among users.
The entity shall: log all activities associated with restricted identities.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.5.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.16; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-2; ISRv3: 5.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.3, 5.5.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The processes used in the context of identity management should ensure that:
a. for identities assigned to persons, each identity is uniquely linked to a single person to ensure accountability for actions performed under that identity.
b. identities assigned to multiple persons (e.g. shared identities) are only permitted when necessary for business or operational reasons and must be subject to dedicated approval and thorough documentation.
c. identities assigned to non-human entities (e.g. service accounts, automated processes) undergo appropriately segregated approval processes and are subject to independent ongoing oversight to ensure their use remains justified and secure.
d. identities are disabled or removed promptly if they are no longer required, such as when associated entities are deleted, no longer in use, or if the person linked to the identity has left the entity or changed roles.
e. within a specific domain, each identity is mapped to a single entity, avoiding the creation of multiple identities for the same entity within the same context to prevent confusion and potential security risks.
f. records of all significant events related to the use and management of user identities and authentication information are maintained, including changes, access attempts, and other relevant activities.
g. the entity has processes in place to handle changes to information related to user identities, including the re-verification of trusted documents linked to a person to maintain the integrity of identity records.
h. when using identities provided or issued by third parties (e.g. social media credentials), the entity ensures these third-party identities meet the required trust levels and that any associated risks are identified, understood, and adequately managed. This may involve implementing controls related to both the third parties and the associated authentication information.

controls.title: Access Rights
controls.description: The entity shall implement a formal access control procedure to manage the provision, modification, and removal of access rights to information and other associated assets.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement a formal access control procedure to manage the provision, modification, and removal of access rights to information and other associated assets.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) establish and formalize procedures for the provisioning and de-provisioning of user access rights.
2) ensure segregation of duties including segregating the roles of approval and implementation of the access rights and separation of conflicting roles.
3) maintain records of access rights for all assets, including identifying any granted special access.
4) immediately revoke access from users who have changed roles or jobs or left the entity following the established procedures.
5) periodically check and revoke access related to temporary and inactive accounts.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: establish and formalize procedures for the provisioning and de-provisioning of user access rights.
The entity shall: ensure segregation of duties including segregating the roles of approval and implementation of the access rights and separation of conflicting roles.
The entity shall: maintain records of access rights for all assets, including identifying any granted special access.
The entity shall: immediately revoke access from users who have changed roles or jobs or left the entity following the established procedures.
The entity shall: periodically check and revoke access related to temporary and inactive accounts.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.2.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.18; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-2, IA-2, IA-4, IA-5, IA-8; ISRv3: 5.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.3, 5.2.4, 5.4, 5.5, 6.1.4.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The access control procedure for user access provisioning and de-provisioning should include:
a. verifying that the user has authorization from the owner of the information system or service for the use of the information system or service; separate approval for access rights from management may also be appropriate.
b. verifying that the level of access granted is appropriate to the business purpose and is consistent with organizational security policy, e.g. it does not compromise segregation of duties.
c. ensuring that access rights are activated (e.g. by service providers) only after authorization procedures are successfully completed.
d. considering segregation of duties, including segregating the roles of approval and implementation of the access rights and separation of conflicting roles.
e. consider giving temporary access rights for a limited time period and revoking them at the expiration date, in particular for temporary personnel or temporary access required by personnel.
f. maintaining a formal record of all persons registered to use systems and service centrally.
g. immediately removing or blocking access rights of users who have changed roles or jobs or left the entity.
h. periodically identifying, and removing or blocking, redundant user IDs and redundant and inactive accounts.
i. ensuring that redundant user IDs are not issued to other users.

controls.title: Privileged Access Rights
controls.description: The entity shall restrict and control the allocation and use of privileged access rights.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall restrict and control the allocation and use of privileged access rights.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) maintain a record of all allocated privileges.
2) ensure that the regular users are not granted with domain or local administrative privileges.
3) ensure that administrator accounts are used only for system administration activities (e.g. no email or web surfing).
4) use multi-factor authentication for all administrative access.
5) prevent the use of single or common passwords across multiple local administrator accounts.
6) log all administrative access activities for audit purposes and ensure these logs are regularly reviewed to detect and respond to any suspicious or unauthorized activities.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: maintain a record of all allocated privileges.
The entity shall: ensure that the regular users are not granted with domain or local administrative privileges.
The entity shall: ensure that administrator accounts are used only for system administration activities (e.g. no email or web surfing).
The entity shall: use multi-factor authentication for all administrative access.
The entity shall: prevent the use of single or common passwords across multiple local administrator accounts.
The entity shall: log all administrative access activities for audit purposes and ensure these logs are regularly reviewed to detect and respond to any suspicious or unauthorized activities.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.2.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.2; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-2, AC-3, AC-6, CM-5; ISRv3: 5.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.3, 5.2.4, 5.4, 5.5.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Multi-user systems that require protection against unauthorized access should have the allocation of privileges controlled through a formal authorization process in accordance with the relevant access control policy. The following steps should be considered:
a. privileged access rights associated with each system, e.g. operating system, database and application, should be identified.
b. privileged access rights should:
• be granted to users strictly on a need-to-use basis and event-by-event basis, according to the access control policy, ensuring users receive the minimum access necessary for their specific roles only when needed.
• not be provided until the formal authorization process is fully completed to prevent unauthorized access.
• be assigned to a separate User ID from the one used for regular daily activities, ensuring that privileged accounts are not used for non-administrative tasks.
c. an authorization process and a record of all privileges allocated should be maintained.
d. a process where users periodically confirm their need for privileged access, helping to ensure that only necessary privileges are retained should be implemented.
e. requirements for expiry of privileged access rights should be defined.
f. the competences of users with privileged access rights should be reviewed regularly in order to verify if they are in line with their duties.
g. specific procedures should be established and maintained in order to avoid the use of generic administration User IDs, according to systems configuration capabilities:
h. for generic administration User IDs, the confidentiality of security credentials should be maintained when shared (changing them frequently and as soon as possible when a privileged user leaves or changes job, communicating them among privileged users with appropriate mechanisms).
i. temporary privileged access should be granted just for the time window necessary to implement approved changes or activities (e.g. for maintenance activities or some critical changes), rather than permanently granting privileged access rights.
j. Break the glass procedures should be established to provide controlled access to critical IT systems in emergencies, such as system outages, failures, or cyber security incidents. These procedures ensure that emergency access accounts are reserved for urgent scenarios requiring privileged access to facilitate immediate troubleshooting and recovery. These accounts must not be used for regular operations and should be governed by formal incident response protocols. All access requests and actions must be documented, monitored, and authorized to maintain security, business continuity, and accountability.
k. ongoing training for users with privileged access should be provided to ensure they understand their responsibilities.

controls.title: Review of User Access Rights
controls.description: The entity shall review users’ access rights.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall review users’ access rights.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) establish an access right review procedure to ensure access rights are reviewed periodically or on any changes in users’ status.
2) periodically check the granted special access to ensure their validity.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: establish an access right review procedure to ensure access rights are reviewed periodically or on any changes in users’ status.
The entity shall: periodically check the granted special access to ensure their validity.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.2.4.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.18; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-2, PE-2; ISRv3: 5.2, 5.2.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The review of access rights should consider the following guidelines:
a. users’ access rights should be reviewed at regular intervals and after any changes, such as promotion, demotion or termination of employment.
b. user access rights should be reviewed and re-allocated when moving from one employment to another within the same entity.
c. authorizations for special privileged access rights should be reviewed at more frequent intervals.
d. privilege allocations should be checked at regular intervals to ensure that unauthorized privileges have not been obtained.
e. changes to privileged accounts should be logged for periodic review.

controls.title: Secure Authentication
controls.description: The entity shall implement secure authentication technologies and procedures.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement secure authentication technologies and procedures.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) implement strong authentication techniques on all information systems.
2) establish the secure log-on and log-off procedures to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.
3) set a maximum session time for logged on users for sensitive systems and applications.
4) terminate inactive sessions after a predefined period of inactivity.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: implement strong authentication techniques on all information systems.
The entity shall: establish the secure log-on and log-off procedures to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.
The entity shall: set a maximum session time for logged on users for sensitive systems and applications.
The entity shall: terminate inactive sessions after a predefined period of inactivity.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.5.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.5; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, IA-6; ISRv3: 5.2.3, 5.2.4.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Even though most applications have secure log-on implemented, a suitable authentication technique should be chosen to substantiate the claimed identity of a user. The strength of authentication should be appropriate for the classification of the information to be accessed.
Where strong authentication and identity verification is required, authentication methods alternative to passwords, such as cryptographic means, smart cards, tokens or biometric means, should be used.
Authentication information should be accompanied by additional authentication factors for accessing critical information systems (also known as multi-factor authentication). Using a combination of multiple authentication factors, such as what you know, what you have and what you are, reduces the possibilities for unauthorized accesses. Multi-factor authentication can be combined with other techniques to require additional factors under specific circumstances, based on predefined rules and patterns, such as access from an unusual location, from an unusual device or at an unusual time.
Biometric authentication information should be invalidated if it is ever compromised. Biometric authentication can be unavailable depending on the conditions of use (e.g. moisture or aging). To prepare for these issues, biometric authentication should be accompanied with at least one alternative authentication technique.
The procedure for logging into a system or application should be designed to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access. The log-on procedure should therefore disclose the minimum of information about the system or application, in order to avoid providing an unauthorized user with any unnecessary assistance. A good log-on procedure should:
a. not display system or application identifiers until the log-on process has been successfully completed.
b. display a general notice warning that the computer should only be accessed by authorized users.
c. not provide help messages during the log-on procedure that would aid an unauthorized user.
d. validate the log-on information only on completion of all input data. If an error condition arises, the system should not indicate which part of the data is correct or incorrect.
e. protect against brute force log-on attempts.
f. log unsuccessful and successful attempts.
g. raise a security event if a potential attempted or successful breach of logon controls is detected.
h. display the following information on completion of a successful log-on:
• date and time of the previous successful log-on.
• details of any unsuccessful log-on attempts since the last successful log-on.
i. Not display a password being entered.
j. not transmit passwords in clear text over a network.
k. terminate inactive sessions after a defined period of inactivity, especially in high risk locations such as public or external areas outside the entity’s security management or on mobile devices.
l. restrict connection times to provide additional security for high-risk applications and reduce the window of opportunity for unauthorized access.
Connection time controls should be considered for sensitive computer applications, especially from high-risk locations, e.g. public or external areas that are outside the entity’s security management. Examples of such restrictions include:
a. using predetermined time slots, e.g. for batch file transmissions, or regular interactive sessions of short duration.
b. restricting connection times to normal office hours if there is no requirement for overtime or extended hours operation.
c. considering re-authentication at timed intervals.
A time-out facility should clear the session screen and also, possibly later, close both application and network sessions after a defined period of inactivity. The time-out delay should reflect the security risks of the area, the classification of the information being handled, and the applications being used, and the risks related to the users of the equipment.
A limited form of time-out facility can be provided for some systems, which clear the screen and prevents unauthorized access but does not close down the application or network sessions.

controls.title: Information Access Restriction
controls.description: The entity shall restrict access to information and other associated assets in accordance with the identity and access management control policy.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall restrict access to information and other associated assets in accordance with the identity and access management control policy.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) ensure access to information and other associated assets is restricted.
2) ensure access restriction is based on the user’s roles and responsibilities.
3) assign the appropriate level of access rights to information and other associated assets.
4) for each user and support personnel, adjust their access control based on specific business needs.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: ensure access to information and other associated assets is restricted.
The entity shall: ensure access restriction is based on the user’s roles and responsibilities.
The entity shall: assign the appropriate level of access rights to information and other associated assets.
The entity shall: for each user and support personnel, adjust their access control based on specific business needs.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.6.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.3; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-3, AC-24; ISRv3: 5.2.1, 5.2.3, 5.2.4.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Access to information and associated assets should be managed according to established identity and access control policies. The following considerations should support effective access restriction:
a. ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ information should not be accessible by unknown user identities or anonymously.
b. public or anonymous access to physical facilities should be granted only to storage locations that do not contain ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ information.
c. mechanisms should be provided for configuring access controls within systems, applications, and services. This includes defining who can access what information and at what level.
d. controls should be in place to manage which data can be accessed by particular users. Access permissions for different identities or groups (e.g. read, write, delete, execute) should be clearly defined and managed.
e. physical or logical controls should be used to isolate sensitive applications, application data, or systems to prevent unauthorized access and maintain data integrity.

controls.title: Remote Access
controls.description: The entity shall use appropriate authentication methods to control access of remote users.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall use appropriate authentication methods to control access of remote users.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) require all remote login (users and administrators) to be done over secure channels.
2) ensure appropriate authentication methods to be used to control access by remote users.
3) control and monitor remote administrator level access, granting it only after necessary approvals.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: require all remote login (users and administrators) to be done over secure channels.
The entity shall: ensure appropriate authentication methods to be used to control access by remote users.
The entity shall: control and monitor remote administrator level access, granting it only after necessary approvals.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.7.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 6.7; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-17, AC-18, AC-20, CA-3, IA-2, IA-8; ISRv3: 5.2.5.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Remote access refers to access to an entity’s information system by a user (or an information system) communicating through an external, non-entity-controlled network (e.g. the Internet) and may refer to “teleworking”, “flexible workplace”, “virtual work environments", “remote maintenance” and “work-from-home” scenarios.
To ensure secure remote access, authentication methods must be robust and effective. Some commonly used methods include:
a. Cryptographic techniques: These can include the use of machine certificates integrated into Virtual Private Network (VPN) solutions to authenticate remote users securely.
b. Hardware tokens: These generate time-based or event-based one-time passwords, providing an additional layer of security.
c. Challenge/response protocols: These require users to respond to specific prompts during login, enhancing the authentication process.
d. Node authentication: For environments with multiple remote users, node authentication using cryptographic techniques like machine certificates can ensure only authorized devices access the network, often integrated into VPN solutions.
The entity should ensure that secure remote access mechanisms are enforced for third-party users or contractors (e.g. those engaged for software development or maintenance). In addition to traditional security measures, entities should implement:
a. Geolocation restrictions: To limit access to specific regions or locations, adding another layer of security for remote connections.
b. IP whitelisting: To restrict access only to authorized IP addresses, reducing the risk of unauthorized access.
c. Monitoring of remote access: Continuous monitoring of remote access activities is crucial to detect any suspicious behavior or potential breaches.
Securing Remote Work Environments
With the rise of remote work, additional security guidelines for telecommuting and flexible work arrangements are necessary. This should include:
a. Device Security: Remote workers must use devices that comply with the entity’s security standards, including encryption, endpoint protection, and secure configurations.
b. Virtual Private Networks (VPNs): All remote connections should be routed through a secure VPN, providing encryption and secure access to internal resources.
c. Multi-factor Authentication (MFA): Remote workers should be required to use MFA, combining something they know (e.g. a password) with something they have (e.g. a hardware token) or something they are (e.g. biometrics).
d. Data Protection: Sensitive data should be stored and transmitted in an encrypted format to protect confidentiality during remote work.
e. Remote Desktop Solutions: Secure remote desktop solutions should be used to ensure that remote employees access the organization's network and applications securely.

controls.title: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.description: The entity shall restrict and control the use of utility programs that might be capable of overriding system and application controls.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall restrict and control the use of utility programs that might be capable of overriding system and application controls.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) restrict use of utility programs only to authorized personnel.
2) monitor the use of utility programs.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: restrict use of utility programs only to authorized personnel.
The entity shall: monitor the use of utility programs.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P4. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.5.4.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: none listed; NIST SP 800-53 r5: AC-3, AC-6; ISRv3: 5.2.3.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The following guidelines for the use of system utilities should be considered:
a. use of identification, authentication, and authorization procedures for system utilities.
b. segregation of system utilities from applications software.
c. limitation of the use of system utilities to the minimum practical number of trusted, authorized users.
d. authorization for ad hoc use of systems utilities.
e. limitation of the availability of system utilities, e.g. for the duration of an authorized change.
f. logging of all use of system utilities.
g. defining and documenting authorization levels for system utilities.
h. removal or disabling of all unnecessary software based utilities and system software.
i. not making system utilities available to users who have access to applications on systems where segregation of duties is required.

controls.title: Allocation of Authentication Information
controls.description: The entity shall control the allocation of user security credentials.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall control the allocation of user security credentials.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) establish a secure process to provide users with security credentials; the procedure shall also include a credential revocation procedure and credential re-allocation.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: establish a secure process to provide users with security credentials; the procedure shall also include a credential revocation procedure and credential re-allocation.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.5.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.17; NIST SP 800-53 r5: IA-5; ISRv3: 5.2.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The allocation and management process should ensure that:
a. personal passwords or personal identification numbers (PINs) generated automatically during enrolment processes as temporary secret authentication information, are non-guessable and unique for each person, and that users are required to change them after the first use.
b. procedures are established to verify the identity of a user prior to providing new, replacement or temporary authentication information.
c. authentication information, including temporary authentication information, is transmitted to users in a secure manner (e.g. over an authenticated and protected channel) and the use of unprotected (clear text) electronic mail messages for this purpose is avoided.
d. users acknowledge receipt of authentication information.
e. default authentication information as predefined or provided by vendors is changed immediately following installation of systems or software.
f. records of significant events concerning allocation and management of authentication information are maintained.
g. passwords are kept and their confidentiality is granted, and that the record-keeping method is approved (e.g. by using an approved password vault tool).

controls.title: User Responsibilities
controls.description: The entity shall require users to use security credentials in line with the entity’s security practices.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall require users to use security credentials in line with the entity’s security practices.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) develop and communicate good practices for use of security credentials.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: develop and communicate good practices for use of security credentials.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P3. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.3.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.17; NIST SP 800-53 r5: IA-5; ISRv3: 5.2.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
All users should be advised to:
a. keep credentials confidential, ensuring that they are not divulged to any other parties, including people of authority.
b. avoid keeping a record (e.g. paper, software file or hand-held device- of security credentials, unless this can be stored securely, and the method of storing has been approved (e.g. password vault).
c. change security credentials whenever there is any indication of their possible compromise.
d. when passwords are used as security credentials, select quality passwords with sufficient minimum length which are:
• easy to remember.
• not based on anything somebody else could easily guess or obtain using person related information, e.g. names, telephone numbers and dates of birth etc.
• not vulnerable to dictionary attacks (i.e. do not consist of words included in dictionaries).
• free of consecutive identical, all-numeric or all-alphabetic characters.
e. change temporary passwords at the first log-on.
f. not share individual user’s security credentials.
g. when passwords are used as security credentials in automated logon procedures, these should not be stored without proper protection.
h. not use the same security credentials for business and non-business purposes.
If users need to access multiple services, systems or platforms, and they are required to maintain multiple separate passwords, they should be advised that they may use a single, quality password (see d) for all services where the user is assured that a reasonable level of protection has been established for the storage of the password within each service, system or platform.

controls.title: User Credentials Management System
controls.description: The entity shall implement a system for managing user credentials.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement a system for managing user credentials.

Sub-Controls:
The user credential management system shall:
1) automate the user credential change procedure ensuring the authenticity of the associate user identity.
2) validate that the changed credentials have sufficient strength for their intended use to ensure quality secret authentication.
3) set a maximum lifetime and reuse conditions.
4) enforce users to change the default password at first login.
5) store credentials in a well-hashed (including “salting”) or encrypted format.
assessment_criteria: The user credential management system shall: automate the user credential change procedure ensuring the authenticity of the associate user identity.
The user credential management system shall: validate that the changed credentials have sufficient strength for their intended use to ensure quality secret authentication.
The user credential management system shall: set a maximum lifetime and reuse conditions.
The user credential management system shall: enforce users to change the default password at first login.
The user credential management system shall: store credentials in a well-hashed (including “salting”) or encrypted format.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T5.2.3, T5.5.3.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.17; NIST SP 800-53 r5: IA-5; ISRv3: 5.2.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
A management system for user credentials should:
a. enforce the use of individual user IDs and credentials to maintain accountability.
b. allow users to select and change their own credentials and include a confirmation procedure to monitor input errors.
c. enforce a choice of quality credentials.
d. enforce credential changes.
e. force users to change temporary credentials at the first log-on.
f. maintain a record of previous user credentials and prevent re-use.
g. not display credentials on the screen when being entered.
h. store credential files separately from application system data.
i. store and transmit credentials in protected (e.g. encrypted or hashed) form.
j. enforce minimum logging attempt before locking out user accounts.

controls.title: Third Party Security Policy
controls.description: The entity shall document and approve a third-party security policy to facilitate the implementation of the associated controls.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall document and approve a third-party security policy to facilitate the implementation of the associated controls.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) define and document a policy providing a framework for third-party risk management.
2) establish the necessary governance to support the implementation of third-party security requirements.
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: define and document a policy providing a framework for third-party risk management.
The entity shall: establish the necessary governance to support the implementation of third-party security requirements.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T6.1.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: none listed; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SR-1; ISRv3: none listed.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The senior leadership of the entity should mandate the establishment of a third party security program with appropriate oversight and direction, and assign resources (budget, people, and technology) for the successful implementation of the program.
The entity should establish, document, and periodically review the effectiveness of policies governing critical aspects of third party security. The entity should identify and ensure compliance with the applicable legal and regulatory requirements (refer to the CSC’s issued National Third Party Security Policy).
The third party security program should establish clear communication channels between stakeholders, such as third-party suppliers, internal departments, and external partners, to ensure effective collaboration and alignment
The entity should provide training and awareness programs for all employees who interact with third-party suppliers.

controls.title: Third-Party Risk Management
controls.description: The entity shall define, document, approve and implement procedures to manage the information security risks associated with the use of the third party’s products or services.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall define, document, approve and implement procedures to manage the information security risks associated with the use of the third party’s products or services.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) classify the entity’s third party suppliers based on the risk they pose to its systems and data.
2) identify and assess the cyber security risks associated with the use of third-party suppliers and their products or services throughout the supply chain.
3) develop and implement strategies to mitigate the risks identified as part of the risk assessment and enable continuous monitoring.
controls.category: T6.2 Management of Third Party and Supply Chain Risks
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: classify the entity’s third party suppliers based on the risk they pose to its systems and data.
The entity shall: identify and assess the cyber security risks associated with the use of third-party suppliers and their products or services throughout the supply chain.
The entity shall: develop and implement strategies to mitigate the risks identified as part of the risk assessment and enable continuous monitoring.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): new control.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.19; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SR-2; ISRv3: 1.7, 6.2.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should identify and implement procedures to address security risks associated with the use of products and services provided by third party. This should also apply to the entity’s use of resources of cloud service providers as well. These procedures should include considerations be implemented by the entity, as well as those the entity requires the third party to implement, for the commencement or for the termination of a third party’s products and services, including:
a. identifying and documenting the types of third parties (e.g. ICT services, logistics, utilities, financial services, ICT infrastructure components) which can affect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the entity's information.
b. establishing how to evaluate and select third party according to the sensitivity of information, products and services (e.g. with market analysis, customer references, review of documents, onsite assessments, certifications).
c. assessing and managing the information security risks associated with:
• the third parties’ use of the entity’s information and other associated assets, including risks originating from potential malicious supplier personnel.
• malfunctioning or vulnerabilities of the products (including software components and subcomponents used in these products) or services provided by the third parties.
The risk mitigation strategy should include appropriate controls and measures to reduce the identified risks to an acceptable level, considering the nature of the vendor's services, the sensitivity of the data or systems involved, and the potential impact of a security breach.
The entity should implement additional measures to mitigate the risks associated with high-risk suppliers, which may include:
a. Enhanced due diligence and background checks.
b. Regular and thorough security assessments, audits, or evaluations to ensure compliance with the defined standards.
c. Periodic vulnerability assessments and penetration testing to identify and address potential vulnerabilities and weaknesses.
d. Proactive monitoring of the high-risk suppliers' activities, such as real-time event monitoring and anomaly detection.
e. Implementing stricter access controls and restrictions to limit their access to ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ information or critical systems.
f. Implementing contractual provisions allowing for increased oversight and accountability, such as the right to conduct on-site visits or inspections.
g. Involving high risk suppliers in resilience assessments and simulations such as red teaming or cyber tabletop exercises.
The entity should periodically re-assess the risks associated with each third-party vendor considering the effectiveness of implemented controls, the vendor's adherence to established security requirements, and any additional risks that may have emerged since the previous risk assessment. The entity should document periodic risk assessment results.
The risk mitigation strategy should be integrated into contractual agreements as appropriate.

controls.title: Third party security assessment during onboarding
controls.description: The entity shall assess third parties' information security posture during third party selection.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall assess third parties' information security posture during third party selection.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) establish reliable criteria for assessing the information security posture of third party suppliers.
2) evaluate the cyber security posture of the third party suppliers in accordance with established criteria.
controls.category: T6.2 Management of Third Party and Supply Chain Risks
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: establish reliable criteria for assessing the information security posture of third party suppliers.
The entity shall: evaluate the cyber security posture of the third party suppliers in accordance with established criteria.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T7.8.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.19; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SR-6; ISRv3: 1.7, 6.2.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should:
a. develop a comprehensive vendor/supplier security assessment template that is aligned to international standards and best practices. The assessment criteria should include relevant topics such as Supplier Governance, Secure Code, Secure Design and Engineering, Information Security, Physical Security, Monitoring and Auditing, Incident Response and Recovery.
b. conduct due diligence checks to verify the validity of the vendor’s cyber security posture prior to onboarding as well as regularly, as determined by the criticality of the third party.

controls.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
controls.description: The entity shall document, approve and implement processes and procedures to manage the information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall document, approve and implement processes and procedures to manage the information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) define and establish clear security requirements for hardware and software procurement.
2) ensure thorough evaluation of hardware and software products prior to procurement.
3) ensure tests are completed prior to accepting new systems into the operational environment.
4) ensure timely and secure upgrades and maintenance of software and hardware in the ICT supply chain.
controls.category: T6.2 Management of Third Party and Supply Chain Risks
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: define and establish clear security requirements for hardware and software procurement.
The entity shall: ensure thorough evaluation of hardware and software products prior to procurement.
The entity shall: ensure tests are completed prior to accepting new systems into the operational environment.
The entity shall: ensure timely and secure upgrades and maintenance of software and hardware in the ICT supply chain.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T7.8.1, T7.8.4.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.21; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SR-3, SR-7, SR-9, SR-10, SR-11; ISRv3: 6.2.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Prior to procurement of hardware and software, the entity should clearly define its security requirements. The entity should define the types of ICT infrastructure components and services provided by third parties which can affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the entity 's information. Procurement requirements should include security criteria for the product, including but not limited to authentication and authorization mechanisms, data encryption, and security protocols. The entity should evaluate third-party software & hardware products and services, against these requirements to ensure that they meet the entity's security standards before procurement.
Other considerations include:
a. The entity should require third parties as per their criticality to provide a software bill of materials (SBOM) or hardware bill of materials (HBOM) for products under consideration for procurement.
b. The entity should use the SBOMs and HBOMs to identify and evaluate all components of the product and assess their potential security risks.
c. The entity should only procure products that have been determined to meet the entity's security standards.
d. The entity should implement processes to ensure that components from third parties are genuine and unaltered from their specification.
The entity should perform acceptance testing (including functional testing, performance testing, and security testing, as appropriate) on all software and hardware prior to deployment to ensure that they meet the entity's security requirements. The entity should:
a. establish testing criteria and test cases based on industry standards, best practices, and the entity's specific security needs.
b. document all testing results and use them to inform decisions about whether to deploy the product, apply additional security controls, or reject the product.
c. do its due diligence to verify the SBOM/HBOMs provided by the vendor prior to deployment, where appropriate.
d. obtain assurance that ICT products achieve required security levels, for example, through formal certification or an evaluation scheme such as the Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement.
e. should obtain assurance that critical components and their origin can be traced throughout the supply chain.
f. obtain assurance that the delivered ICT products are functioning as expected without any unexpected or unwanted features.
g. define rules for sharing of information regarding the supply chain and any potential issues and compromises among the entity and third parties.
The entity should:
a. ensure that all software and hardware upgrades and maintenance activities are carried out in a timely manner to maintain the security of the supply chain.
b. require suppliers to provide advance notice of any planned upgrades or maintenance activities impacting the entity's systems.
c. ensure that upgrades and maintenance activities are tested in a test environment before they are deployed in the production environment.
d. ensure that any vulnerabilities discovered during the upgrade or maintenance process are documented, prioritized, and addressed in a timely manner prior to deployment.
The entity should establish secure decommissioning and disposal processes for all software and hardware products that have reached end-of-life.
The entity should identify an alternative supplier and the process to transfer software and competence to the alternative third party, in case of suppliers no longer being in business or third parties no longer providing these components due to technology advancements or other organizational decisions.

controls.title: Addressing information security within third party agreements
controls.description: The entity shall establish and agree upon relevant information security requirements with each third party based on the type of relationship with third party.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish and agree upon relevant information security requirements with each third party based on the type of relationship with third party.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) embed information security requirements in contracts with third party suppliers.
2) ensure third party suppliers are compliant with applicable laws and regulations through contractual obligation.
controls.category: T6.2 Management of Third Party and Supply Chain Risks
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: embed information security requirements in contracts with third party suppliers.
The entity shall: ensure third party suppliers are compliant with applicable laws and regulations through contractual obligation.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): M1.3.7, T6.3.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.2; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SA-4, SR-3; ISRv3: 1.5, 1.7, 6.2, 13.2.4.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should, in line with outcomes from its risk assessments, include specific information security requirements in contracts and agreements with suppliers. The following requirements should be considered for inclusion in the agreements in order to satisfy the identified information security requirements:
a. clearly communicating and including cyber security requirements in contracts with suppliers and require that suppliers pass these requirements down to their sub-contractors.
b. including appropriate step-in rights in contracts to secure continued access to data and critical services.
c. contractually requiring that the supplier provide timely notification to the entity in the event of a security incident, data breach, or any other cyber security-related event that may impact the entity's data or systems.
d. requiring suppliers to disclose any identified vulnerabilities or security weaknesses in their products, systems, or services that may impact the entity's security posture in a timely manner.
e. including clauses or contracts to protect its data such as Non-Disclosure Agreements and Intellectual Property protection clauses.
f. specifying in its contacts, the conditions under which it may terminate agreements with its suppliers in the event of non-compliance with cyber security requirements or breaches of contractual obligations and should include provisions for the secure return or disposal of the entity's data and assets upon termination or completion of the engagement.
g. explicitly stating in its contracts that suppliers must comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations.
h. including relevant provisions for sub-contracting, including the controls that need to be implemented, such as agreement on the use of sub-suppliers (e.g. requiring to have them under the same obligations of the supplier, requiring to have a list of sub-suppliers and notification before any change.
i. including training and awareness requirements for specific procedures and information security requirements (e.g. for incident response, authorization procedures).
The entity may also consider the following as part of contractual obligations:
a. include any screening requirements, for the supplier’s personnel, including responsibilities for conducting the screening and notification procedures if screening has not been completed or if the results give cause for doubt or concern.
b. require evidence and assurance of attestations for relevant information security requirements related to the third-party processes and/ or an independent report on effectiveness of controls.
c. ensure that backup arrangements are aligned with the entity’s needs (in terms of frequency and type and storage location).
d. ensure the availability of an alternate facility (i.e. disaster recovery site) not subject to the same threats as the primary facility and considerations for fall back controls (alternate controls) in the event primary controls fail.
e. include a method of securely destroying the entity’s information stored by the third party as soon as it is no longer required.
f. ensure that at the end of the contract, handover support to another third party or to the entity itself.

controls.title: Monitoring, review, and change management of third party services
controls.description: The entity shall regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage changes in third party information security practices and service delivery.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage changes in third party information security practices and service delivery.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) implement a monitoring program to ensure that its suppliers adhere to the defined contractual cyber security requirements.
2) conduct assessments, audits, or evaluations to verify suppliers' compliance with the specified security controls and measures.
3) implement a change management in supplier information security practices and service delivery.
controls.category: T6.2 Management of Third Party and Supply Chain Risks
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: implement a monitoring program to ensure that its suppliers adhere to the defined contractual cyber security requirements.
The entity shall: conduct assessments, audits, or evaluations to verify suppliers' compliance with the specified security controls and measures.
The entity shall: implement a change management in supplier information security practices and service delivery.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P2. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T6.2.3.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.22; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SA-9, SR-6, RA-9, SR-7; ISRv3: 6.2.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should:
a. independently gather and analyze threat intelligence to identify emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and indicators of compromise that may impact its supply chain.
b. establish logging and auditing mechanisms to monitor the activities of third-party suppliers accessing its information or critical systems. The entity should retain logs to facilitate the investigation of security incidents, identify potential vulnerabilities, and ensure accountability.
Monitoring compliance with established information security requirements for each type of supplier and type of access, including third-party review and product validation, should be undertaken. The entity should mitigate non-compliance of a supplier, whether this was detected through monitoring or by other means and monitor service performance levels to verify compliance with the agreements.
The entity should also monitor changes made by third party including:
a. enhancements to the current services offered.
b. development of any new applications and systems.
c. modifications or updates of the supplier’s policies and procedures.
d. new or changed controls to resolve information security incidents and to improve information security.
e. changes and enhancement to networks.
f. use of new technologies.
g. adoption of new products or newer versions or releases.
h. new development tools and environments.
i. changes to physical location of service facilities.
j. change of sub- third parties.
k. sub-contracting to another supplier.
The entity should also consider mechanisms to review information security aspects of the supplier’s relationships with its own third parties and ensure that the third party maintains sufficient service capability together with workable plans to meet agreed service continuity levels.

controls.title: Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance Policy
controls.description: The entity shall document and approve an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall document and approve an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy.

Sub-Controls:
Entity shall document and implement an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy that shall:
1) be appropriate to the relationship of the entity and all internal and external parties involved in the process.
2) outline the roles and responsibilities.
3) provide the framework for integrating information security controls throughout the lifecycle of acquiring, designing, developing, implementing, and maintaining information systems, whether developed in-house or outsourced.
controls.domain: T7 Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance
controls.category: T7.1 Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance Policy
assessment_criteria: Entity shall document and implement an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy that shall: be appropriate to the relationship of the entity and all internal and external parties involved in the process.
Entity shall document and implement an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy that shall: outline the roles and responsibilities.

Entity shall document and implement an information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance policy that shall: provide the framework for integrating information security controls throughout the lifecycle of acquiring, designing, developing, implementing, and maintaining information systems, whether developed in-house or outsourced.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P3. Control type: Preventive, Detective, Corrective. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T7.1.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: none listed; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SA-3, SA-15, SA-17; ISRv3: 6.1.6, 8.1.1.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The information systems acquisition, development and maintenance policy shall facilitate the implementation of the associated controls to integrate information security requirements into the software life cycle of information systems that contain protected data. The policy should contain in addition to the required sub-controls:
a. separation of development, test and production environments.
b. guidance on the security in the software development life cycle:
• security in the software development methodology.
• secure coding guidelines for each programming language used.
c. security requirements in the specification and design phase.
d. security checkpoints in projects
e. system and security testing, such as regression testing, code scan and penetration tests.
f. secure repositories for source code and configuration.
g. security in the version control.
h. required application security knowledge and training.
i. developers’ capability for preventing, finding and fixing vulnerabilities.
j. licensing requirements and alternatives to ensure cost-effective solutions while avoiding future licensing issues.
The entity should adopt and integrate its policies with modern development methodologies, such as DevSecOps, to ensure ongoing security throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). This can be achieved by:
a. Embedding security considerations early in the development process:
• Conducting threat modeling during the design phase.
• Implementing secure coding practices.
b. Automating security checks within the CI/CD pipeline, such as:
• Static Application Security Testing (SAST).
• Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST).
• Software Composition Analysis.
The information systems acquisition, development and maintenance policy can be included as part of the general information security policy, in a single policy document, or can be represented by multiple policies reflecting the complex nature of certain entities.

controls.title: Application Security Requirements
controls.description: The entity shall identify, specify, and approve the information security requirements when developing or acquiring applications.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall identify, specify, and approve the information security requirements when developing or acquiring applications.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) identify and address information security requirements when developing or acquiring applications.
2) implement application security requirements depending on the purpose of the application, including controls for transactional services, electronic commerce, and payment applications, where applicable.
controls.domain: T7 Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance
controls.category: T7.2 Security Requirements of Information Systems
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: identify and address information security requirements when developing or acquiring applications.

The entity shall: implement application security requirements depending on the purpose of the application, including controls for transactional services, electronic commerce, and payment applications, where applicable.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Always applicable. Implementation priority: P1. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T4.3.1, T4.3.2, T7.2.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.26; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SA-4; ISRv3: 6.1.6, 6.7, 6.7.1, 6.7.2, 8.1.2, 8.2.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Application security requirements should be identified and specified. These requirements are usually determined through a risk assessment. The requirements should be developed with the support of information security specialists. Application security requirements can cover a wide range of topics, depending on the purpose of the application.
Application security requirements should include, as applicable:
a. level of trust in the identity of entities [e.g. through authentication (refer T5.3.1).
b. identifying the type of information and classification level to be processed by the application.
c. need for segregation of access and level of access to data and functions in the application.
d. resilience against malicious attacks or unintentional disruptions [e.g. protection against buffer overflow or structured query language (SQL) injections].
e. legal, statutory and regulatory requirements in the jurisdiction where the transaction is generated, processed, completed or stored.
f. need for privacy associated with all parties involved.
g. the protection requirements of any ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ information.
h. protection of data while being processed, in transit and at rest.
i. need to securely encrypt communications between all involved parties.
j. input controls, including integrity checks and input validation.
k. automated controls (e.g. approval limits or dual approvals).
l. output controls, also considering who can access outputs and its authorization.
m. restrictions around the content of "free-text" fields, as these can lead to uncontrolled storage of ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ data (e.g. personal data).
n. requirements derived from the business process, such as transaction logging and monitoring, and non-repudiation requirements.
o. requirements mandated by other security controls (e.g. interfaces to logging and monitoring or data leakage detection systems).
p. error message handling.
Transactional services
Additionally, for applications offering transactional services between the entity and a partner, the following should be considered when identifying information security requirements:
a. the level of trust each party requires in each other’s claimed identity.
b. the level of trust required in the integrity of information exchanged or processed and the mechanisms for identification of lack of integrity (e.g. cyclic redundancy check, hashing, digital signatures).
c. authorization processes associated with who can approve contents of issue or sign key transactional documents.
d. confidentiality, integrity, proof of dispatch and receipt of key documents and non-repudiation (e.g. contracts associated with tendering and contract processes).
e. the confidentiality and integrity of any transactions (e.g. orders, delivery address details and confirmation of receipts).
f. requirements on how long to maintain a transaction confidential.
g. insurance and other contractual requirements.
Electronic ordering and payment applications
Additionally, for applications involving electronic ordering and payment, the following should be considered:
a. requirements for maintaining the confidentiality and integrity of order information.
b. the degree of verification appropriate to verify payment information supplied by a customer.
c. avoidance of loss or duplication of transaction information.
d. storing transaction details outside of any publicly accessible environment (e.g. on a storage platform existing on the organizational intranet, and not retained and exposed on electronic storage media directly accessible from the internet).
e. when a trusted authority is involved, such as for issuing and maintaining digital signatures or certificates, security is seamlessly integrated and embedded throughout the entire certificate or signature management process.
Digital services
For applications used to provide digital services, the following should be considered:
a. requirements for maintaining the confidentiality and integrity of digital services.
b. requirements for availability of digital services.
c. compliance with the laws, regulations, government policies, and information security and business continuity requirements.
d. requirements on storing and retaining customer information.
e. the level of trust required in the integrity of information exchanged or processed and the mechanisms for identification of lack of integrity.
f. strong mechanism for authentication and authorization.
Other information
Applications accessible via networks are subject to a range of network-related threats, such as fraudulent activities, contract disputes or disclosure of information to the public, incomplete transmission, misrouting, unauthorized message alteration, duplication or replay. Therefore, detailed risk assessments and careful determination of controls are indispensable. Controls required often include cryptographic methods for authentication and secure data transfer.

controls.title: Secure system engineering principles
controls.description: The entity shall establish, document, approve, maintain, and implement principles for engineering secure systems throughout all information system development activities.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish, document, approve, maintain, and implement principles for engineering secure systems throughout all information system development activities.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) establish and document secure engineering principles for information system engineering activities.
2) ensure that engineering principles are consistently applied across architecture layers (business, data, applications and technology).
controls.domain: T7 Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance
controls.category: T7.2 Security Requirements of Information Systems
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: establish and document secure engineering principles for information system engineering activities.
The entity shall: ensure that engineering principles are consistently applied across architecture layers (business, data, applications and technology).
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P4. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): new control.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 8.27; NIST SP 800-53 r5: SA-8; ISRv3: 6.1.6, 8.3.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Security engineering principles should be established, documented and applied to information system engineering activities. Security should be designed into all architecture layers (business, data, applications and technology). New technology should be analyzed for security risks and the design should be reviewed against known attack patterns.
Secure engineering principles provide guidance on user authentication techniques, secure session control and data validation and sanitization.
Secure system engineering principles should include an analysis of:
a. the full range of security controls required to protect information and systems against identified threats.
b. the capabilities of security controls to prevent, detect, or respond to security events.
c. specific security controls required by particular business processes (e.g. encryption of ‘Confidential/Restricted’ or ‘Secret’ or ‘Top Secret’ information, integrity checking, and digitally signing information).
d. where and how security controls are to be applied (e.g. by integrating with a security architecture and the technical infrastructure).
e. how individual security controls (manual and automated) work together to produce an integrated set of controls.
Security engineering principles should consider:
a. the need to integrate with a security architecture.
b. technical security infrastructure [e.g. public key infrastructure (PKI), identity and access management (IAM), data leakage prevention, and dynamic access management].
c. capability of the entity to develop and support the chosen technology.
d. cost, time, and complexity of meeting security requirements.
e. current good practices.
Secure system engineering should involve:
a. the use of security architecture principles, such as “security by design”, “defense in depth”, “security by default”, “default deny”, “fail securely”, “distrust input from external applications”, “security in deployment”, “assume breach”, "least privilege", “usability and manageability” and “least functionality”.
b. a security-oriented design review to help identify information security vulnerabilities, ensure security controls are specified and meet security requirements.
c. documentation and formal acknowledgment of security controls that do not fully meet requirements (e.g. due to overriding safety requirements).
d. hardening of systems.
The entity should establish a comprehensive process to ensure that all newly engineered systems adhere to the entity's approved security engineering principles and architecture. This can be achieved by setting up architecture review boards, which will evaluate and approve system designs for compliance with security standards.
The entity should establish a cyber security reference architecture to identify and manage its cyber security capabilities. Security blueprints should be developed for key cyber security domains such as identity and access management, network security, data security, and DevSecOps. These blueprints should be used to guide architectural discussions when new technologies, solutions, or systems are deployed or developed.
.

controls.title: Secure Coding
controls.description: The entity shall apply secure coding practices for software development.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall apply secure coding practices for software development.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) ensure that secure coding practices are documented, approved, and utilized during software development.
2) conduct security testing during and after deployment utilizing automated testing tools.
3) ensure that developers are equipped with the required application security knowledge and training.
controls.domain: T7 Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Maintenance
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: ensure that secure coding practices are documented, approved, and utilized during software development.
The entity shall: conduct security testing during and after deployment utilizing automated testing tools.
The entity shall: ensure that developers are equipped with the required application security knowledge and training.
controls.ai_notes:
